title: Never say "no," but rarely say "yes": qualify your yes so it funds what you want
summary: Jason Cohen resolves the tension between startup focus and experimentation by never refusing outright, but attaching terms to "yes" so strong that acceptance funds your real goals and rejection costs nothing. He illustrates with $100/hr consulting, WP Engine's large-blogger deals, and $2,500/day code-review trips at Smart Bear.

principles.text: Don't say "no" to off-strategy opportunities; say a heavily qualified "yes" so you can still explore and learn if you were wrong.
principles.quote: Here's what I do: I never say "no." But I carefully qualify "yes."

principles.text: Set the terms so both outcomes win: if they accept, it more than compensates for the distraction; if they decline, it wasn't a fit anyway.
principles.quote: If they say "yes," you're happy because the terms or money are *so good*, it more than compensates for the distraction, perhaps funding the thing you really want to do.

principles.text: Price unwanted work far above your normal rate; people may well accept. Quoting 4x his rate got a yes instead of a laugh.
principles.quote: The difference between saying "no" and getting $150 for about two hours of my life was all in how I phrased "yes."

principles.text: Quote a distracting big customer high enough to cover a whole person's salary, since the deal will eat much of that person's time.
principles.quote: This deal needs to be big enough to not only make a reasonable profit on the operating expenses, but pay for an entire developer's salary

principles.text: Anchor your qualified yes to funding something you already want to do, such as a hire, runway, or marketing efforts.
principles.quote: "Yes" if it pays for an entire additional person.

principles.text: Treat distracting revenue like funding: it must be transformative to be worth the interruption, otherwise let the price filter it out.
principles.quote: Funding is always a distraction from actually running your business, so the amount of money you get must be transformative to the business.
